focus: What evidence would justify production changes involving singleWriterReadCache or gateway rescans, and how should their runtime-behavior risk be separated from test-only speed work?

ruledOut: Enabling a gateway cache without profile and multi-writer evidence.
Removing fresh-head, locked-append, or post-append projection reads without preserved correctness proofs.

label: The singleWriterReadCache option is opt-in and defaults off. Its documented safety condition is that the ledger instance remains the sole writer for its lifetime: a cache hit skips the cross-process lock, so another process’s append can remain invisible until a miss triggers a rescan. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/authorized-ledger/authorized-ledger-types.ts:104] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/authorized-ledger/append-only-ledger.ts:383] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/authorized-ledger/append-only-ledger.ts:399]

The cache is already enabled for the long-lived per-lineage effect ledger, whose source says it has one owning process. Its focused unit tests assert that repeated reads avoid extra locks, an instance’s own append invalidates the memo, cached events and heads match lock-per-read results, and the default-off path locks on every read. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/fanout-effect-dispatch.ts:411] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/deep-loop/fanout-effect-dispatch.ts:420] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/tests/unit/ledger-read-cache.vitest.ts:130] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/tests/unit/ledger-read-cache.vitest.ts:154] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/tests/unit/ledger-read-cache.vitest.ts:164] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/tests/unit/ledger-read-cache.vitest.ts:198]

The CLI gateway leaves the cache option unset (therefore default-off) and performs freshness-sensitive reads around the append: it reads a current head before event preparation; the gateway reads verified events for provenance and idempotency and a verified head before authorization; the append rescans under the exclusive lock; projection then reads the head and events again. These reads support replay detection, current-head authorization and fencing, and refreshed state, so removing them requires a measured design that preserves those contracts. The packet excludes additional production changes that alter runtime behavior and records that fixture sharing was a test-only cut. The current code’s existing single-writer cache does not contradict that boundary: it is already present and narrowly used, while a new gateway cache or rescan reduction remains unproven. Justify another production change only with profile evidence that the affected scans materially contribute to the target suite and with separate tests for stale cross-process reads, append visibility, fencing and retries, and projection parity; keep test-fixture reuse in a test-only change.
